title: Agent Pulse
description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

inputs.dailyInsight: reported, date-owned Agent Pulse decision brief

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — September 23, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: QwenLM/qwen-code is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: QwenLM/qwen-code leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: QwenLM/qwen-code — 11 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 27.7 below its current daily pace, with 15 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 102 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
microsoft/agent-framework — No same-day commit after 109 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Test whether sandbox policy survives a settings save
dailyInsight.insight: Qwen Code's new Linux tool boundary depends on operator policy being present at startup. A public follow-up records a settings replacement gap that can make the policy temporarily absent.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The settings writer moves the existing settings file to a backup before installing its replacement. The policy reader treats a missing file as an empty scope. This is distinct from malformed or torn settings reads, which the merged change now rejects.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A command confinement test can pass while a concurrent settings save leaves a different session without the intended policy. Operators need to test admission as well as enforcement.

actions.audience: Teams evaluating Qwen Code's Linux tool sandbox
actions.label: Add a policy-continuity acceptance case
actions.instruction: In a disposable Linux test environment containing PR #12267, establish the configured boundary with qwen sandbox --verify, then test settings saves concurrent with new session startup using harmless temporary-file probes. Require either the intended policy or an explicit refusal. Do not run this experiment against personal settings or sensitive files.
actions.effort: 30–60 minutes with an existing Linux test setup

receipts.title: Merged public tool-execution boundary
receipts.supports: Operator-owned executionSandbox policy, absent-file handling, fail-closed malformed settings and explicit rejection of unported integrations.

receipts.title: Settings continuity remains in the follow-up
receipts.supports: The author retains the rename gap, attributed concurrent-start experiment and required regression as open hardening work.

confidence.basis: The settings writer and reader agree with the public follow-up mechanism; the timing-dependent reproduction is attributed to the upstream reviewer.

dailyInsight.limitation: We did not independently reproduce the race, map installed releases or measure deployment incidence. Successful upstream isolation probes remain counterevidence to a general claim that the tool sandbox fails.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise the call when the shipped writer keeps policy continuously visible and a concurrent reader-and-writer regression rules out an unconfined startup, or if another enforced scope demonstrably prevents the reported gap in the evaluated configuration.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Closure of issue #12417's atomic settings-write work with platform-specific evidence and a regression that exercises real concurrent startup.
